newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE EXCLUDES HANDLOWY EMPLOYEE TRANCHE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE EXCLUDES HANDLOWY EMPLOYEE TRANCHE.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse approved for trade only 60,359,000 shares of Bank Handlowy's initial public offering from among the 65 million shares already approved for public trade, the bourse said in a Wednesday statement.

The Polish Securities Commission approved for public trade Handlowy's 65 million shares and in its issue prospectus the bank offered the public 61,750,000 shares, as 3,250,000 shares would be retained by the treasury for restitution claims.

Maciej Bombol, the privatisation adviser to Handlowy's board, told Reuters that the bourse approved for trade 3,250,000 shares which the treasury will retain and left out the 4,641,000 shares of the employee tranche.
"The employee shares were not approved for trade by the bourse, while shares from the treasury's restitution reserve were," Bombol said.
Handlowy is to sell the shares to employees at a nominal price of four zlotys each.
The subscription in the individual investor tranche of 9,750,000 shares and institutional investor tranche of 19,500,000 shares will be between May 26 and June 13.
The bank will also offer 28,859,000 shares to so-called stable investors who have to keep their shares for at least three years.
The bank is to announce the price bracket for the tranches on May 23 at the latest.
Shares of Handlowy, Poland's biggest commercial bank, for individual investors will be allotted at a special bourse session on June 21.

The allotment of shares to institutional investors will be no later than on June 24 with preference to those bidders who want to buy shares and not only the bank's Global Depositary Receipts, which will also be on offer.
